{{nihongo|'''Igami Shrine'''|猪上神社}} is a Shinto shrine enshrined in Shigibata, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|Q971003|qid=Q971003}}{{ill|Heguri, Nara|ar|هيغوري|arz|هيجورى|ceb|Heguri-chō|eo|Heguri|es|Heguri (Nara)|fa|هگوری، نارا|fr|Heguri|hy|Հեգուրի|it|Heguri|ja|平群町|ko|헤구리정|ms|Heguri, Nara|my|ဟဲဂုရိမြို့၊ နာရ|pl|Heguri|ru|Хегури|simple|Heguri, Nara|sv|Heguri|tl|Heguri, Nara|tr|Heguri|uk|Хеґурі (Нара)|ur|ہیگوری، نارا|zh|平群町|qid=Q1346790}}, and is listed in the ''{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}} as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}. {{nihongo|'''Igami Shrine'''|猪上神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

== Overview ==
It is located just over about 100 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573}} past the Niō Gate of Shigisan {{ill|Chōgosonshi-ji|arz|تشوجوسونشى جى|fr|Chōgosonshi-ji|ja|朝護孫子寺|zh|朝護孫子寺|qid=Q11092571}}, the head temple of the {{ill|Shigisan Shingon-shū|ja|信貴山真言宗|zh|信貴山真言宗|qid=Q9393338}}, on the immediate right side of the approach path.

Since ancient times, it has stood within the precincts of {{ill|Mount Shigi|arz|جبل مونت شيجى|ceb|Shigi San|fr|Mont Shigi|ja|信貴山|lld|Mont Shigi|qid=Q6923605}} and served as the {{ill|Chinjusha|fr|Chinjusha|it|Chinjusha|ja|鎮守社|qid=Q13479654}} of Chōgosonshi-ji.

It is said that the site of the {{ill|Kyōzō|de|Kyōzō|es|Kyōzō|fr|Kyōzō|ja|経蔵 (建築)|qid=Q1325051|lt=sutra repository}} located between the water pavilion at the foot of the main hall stone steps and the Reihō Hall was the former shrine site. The shrine was widely revered under the name “Shigisan Igami Daimyōjin”<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book|title=History of Heguri Town|publisher=Heguri Town Office|pages=661–664}}</ref>.

In the 3rd year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} (1870), due to the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinbutsu bunri edict}}, the shrine was moved outside the [https://kotobank.jp/word/総門･惣門-2056818 sōmon (main gate)] to Mount Kengai. Later, in the 11th year of {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}, it was relocated to its present position beside the approach path<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book|editor=Heguri Town History Editorial Committee|title=History of Heguri Town|publisher=Heguri Town Office|date=1976-04|ncid=BN04492478|page=661–664}}</ref>.

The {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}} are {{ill|Prince Ametarashihiko|ja|天足彦国押人命|qid=Q11443593}}. Within the main hall, Ame-tarashihiko-no-Mikoto is enshrined on the left side facing inward, and Kuni-oshihito-no-Mikoto on the right.

Although the origins are not clearly transmitted, the ''[https://kotobank.jp/word/阿娑縛抄-25051 Asabashō]'' from the second year of {{ill|Kōan (Kamakura period)|de|Kōan (Kamakura-Zeit)|fa|کوآن (دوره)|fr|Ère Kōan (Kamakura)|ia|Koan (prime)|id|Kōan|ja|弘安|ko|고안 (1278년)|ru|Коан (Камакура)|simple|Kōan (Kamakura period)|sr|Коан (Камакура период)|sv|Kōan (Kamakura)|tr|Kōan (Kamakura)|zh|弘安|qid=Q389180}} records that during the {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} era, when Myōren, who revitalized Mount Shigi, prayed for the expansion of the temple buildings, a sacred boar appeared. Because the construction was completed overnight, it is said that this sacred boar was enshrined.

Mount Shigi was formerly called Mount Inoue, and one theory holds that “Inoue Shrine” derives from an {{ill|Ateji|Q754018|qid=Q754018}} for Inoue. Another theory suggests that, based on the location of the former shrine site, an “Ogami Shrine” that worshipped the {{ill|Chinjusha|fr|Chinjusha|it|Chinjusha|ja|鎮守社|qid=Q13479654}} Mount Shigi later underwent a change in pronunciation and was written using {{ill|phonetic borrowing|Q10888308|qid=Q10888308}}, becoming “Inoue Shrine.”

== Access ==

== By public transportation ==

* From {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125|lt=JR}} {{ill|Yamatoji Line|Q1151659|qid=Q1151659}} “{{ill|Ōji Station (Nara)|Q856582|qid=Q856582}},” take a {{ill|Nara Kotsu Bus Lines|Q11445000|qid=Q11445000}} bus bound for Shigisanmon, get off at Shigi Ōhashi, then about a 5-minute walk. (Also via Nara Kōtsū bus from {{ill|Ikoma Line|Q900218|qid=Q900218}} “{{ill|Shigisanshita Station|Q7496434|qid=Q7496434}}”)
* From {{ill|Osaka Line|Q1052545|qid=Q1052545}} “{{ill|Kawachi-Yamamoto Station|Q6379464|qid=Q6379464}},” take the {{ill|Shigi Line|Q874150|qid=Q874150|lt=Shigi Line}} to “{{ill|Shigisanguchi Station|Q7496433|qid=Q7496433}},” transfer to the {{ill|Nishi-Shigi Cable Line|Q8140289|qid=Q8140289|lt=cable car}}, then transfer to a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|Q18636319|qid=Q18636319}} at “{{ill|Takayasuyama Station|Q7677479|qid=Q7677479}},” and get off at Shigisanmon.

== By private car ==

* Via the {{ill|Hanna road|Q11656692|qid=Q11656692}} from the Ikoma trailhead, then the {{ill|Shigi-Ikoma Skyline|Q11386259|qid=Q11386259}}.
* Kashiwara City Road Shigi-Ōgata Line: From the Ōgata-minami intersection on {{ill|Japan National Route 170|Q6156852|qid=Q6156852}} (old road) ({{ill|Kashiwara|Q873583|qid=Q873583}}), head east, pass the summit of {{ill|Mount Takao|Q11669240|qid=Q11669240|lt=Mount Takao}}, the vicinity of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shigisan Nodoka Village}}, and proceed to the area near Shigisanmon.
* Via {{ill|Nara Prefectural Road Route 236|Q11445341|qid=Q11445341}}.
* Via {{ill|Osaka Prefectural Road Route 183|Q11441300|qid=Q11441300}}.
* Parking fee: 500 yen (passenger cars / once per day)
